subject: Pinwave failsafe check & quiet-window negotiation for OctavoAI private cluster
messages:
From: Tom Walters <tom.walters@octavoai.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.company
Cc: Ben Stanford <ben.stanford@octavoai.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coordinating maintenance window + pinwave failsafe check

Hi Jasmine,

We want to schedule the next maintenance window for our private VPC cluster to apply the Q2 micropatch set. Before we lock dates, two asks from Octavo:

1) Can Redwood run a pre-flight "pinwave failsafe" check to ensure that our pinned versions (v12.3.4) can be bumped to the intended micro-release without breaking the model-serving KV cache?
2) We need to negotiate a quiet window that minimizes TPS impact — our billing cycles peak Mon-Fri 10:00-18:00 ET, so weekend windows are preferred but we have one scheduled merchant migration last weekend of June which complicates things.

I've attached our current maintenance matrix (octavo_maintenance_window.xlsx). Ben and I are available for a quick 30m call next week to walk through dependencies.

Goals for the thread: proposed quiet window, required canary scope, rollback SLA (RTO target), and a simple checklist for the pre-flight check.

Thanks,
Tom

--
Tom Walters
Head of Platform Engineering | OctavoAI
+1 415 555 0123
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.company>
To: Tom Walters <tom.walters@octavoai.com>, Ben Stanford <ben.stanford@octavoai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.company
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating maintenance window + pinwave failsafe check

Tom — thanks for the context and the spreadsheet. Quick answers up front: weekend window looks best; we can do a pre-flight automated failsafe check and a limited canary prior to fleet-wide roll.

Proposed timeline (short):
- Pre-flight failsafe run (automated): Fri 2025-06-27 02:00-03:30 PT — tooling will validate pinned artifacts, run a dry-run start/stop, and surface KV cache mismatches.
- Canary slice (small subset, warm traffic): Sat 2025-06-28 01:00-04:00 PT — 5% of traffic, manual approval gate.
- Fleet apply (staggered slices): Sun 2025-06-29 02:00-08:00 PT — 20% slices with 30m observation windows.

Checkpoints we need from your side:
- Agreement on the canary SLA (are you okay with 30m observation windows and an immediate abort if latency P95 increases > 50%?).
- Confirmation that Octavo can divert non-critical traffic and pause scheduled batch jobs during the windows.

I've attached our "pinwave-failsafe-checklist.pdf" which lists the exact pre-flight probes we run (KV checksum, prefix cache warm-start, model-compat smoke). Karthik — looping you for kernel/quantization implications and whether we need a special build for this customer's pinned runtime.

If that schedule looks good we'll circulate a calendar invite and a short runbook.

Best,
Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.company
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.company>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.company
Cc: Tom Walters <tom.walters@octavoai.com>, Ben Stanford <ben.stanford@octavoai.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.company
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating maintenance window + pinwave failsafe check

Quick technical addendum — reading their matrix, two risk items to call out:

1) Quantization/Kernel mismatch: Octavo's pinned runtime uses the older fused-attn kernels. The micropatch introduces an alternate kernel selector that may change scheduling for long-context models. Our pre-flight must include a long-tail latency test (1% percentile) using the production prompt set.

2) KV cache thermalization: During canary slices we should enable KV-prefix warm-cache and a shadow replay for 10 minutes to ensure no cold-start misses propagate. If the shadow replay finds >0.1% cache-miss rate compared to baseline we should abort.

Rollback mechanics (what I recommend):
- Immediate: Cancel ongoing apply, roll traffic to the canary-compatible model variant (pinned rollback image).
- 15m: Snapshot node volumes + re-pin service manifest to previous tag.
- 45m: If snapshot restore fails, failover to dedicated fallback region (if Octavo has reserved capacity) — this is a last resort and requires pre-approval.

I will prepare the lightweight test harness for the pre-flight (long-tail latency script + cache-replay) and drop in the runbook. Naomi — can you confirm ops staffing for the 27–29 June nights?

-Karthik
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.company>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.company>, jasmine_liu@redwood.company
Cc: Tom Walters <tom.walters@octavoai.com>, Ben Stanford <ben.stanford@octavoai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating maintenance window + pinwave failsafe check

Confirmed from ops: we can staff the nights at the proposed times (Pre-flight 6/27, canary 6/28, fleet 6/29). Two notes:

- Approval matrix: we need Octavo's primary on-call reachable during the canary approval gate. Please provide a mobile contact.
- Doc stamps: before we proceed we need a signed maintenance authorization (DocuSign) that includes the rollback SLA and the fallback-region pre-approval. Tom — I'll send the DocuSign link; please sign by EOD Tue 2025-06-17 to lock the window.

Operational checklist (high level):
- T-72h: Share final manifests and traffic routing rules.
- T-24h: Dry run of pre-flight probes against a staging copy.
- T-1h: Pause non-critical cron jobs, enable extra logging retention for 48h.
- During: 30m observation windows between slices; immediate abort on any P95 latency regression >50% or cache-miss >0.1%.

Tom — can you confirm the primary contact and whether Octavo approves the rollback ladder above? If approved we'll open the maintenance ticket and circulate the invite.

Thanks,
Naomi
